title: Disparities in Access to Occupational and Physical Therapy Among U.S. Adults With Functional Limitations
content: Adults with functional limitations rely on occupational and physical therapy (OT/PT) to maintain daily function, yet national evidence on who reaches these services is limited. Using Medical Expenditure Panel Survey data from 2000 to 2016 (101,441 person-years), survey-weighted models examined any OT/PT use and visit volume among users. Black, Hispanic, and Asian/Other adults had 16% to 23% lower adjusted odds of use than White adults, uninsured adults had less than half the odds, and use rose with income. Visit volume did not differ by race, insurance, or income. Equity efforts should target referral, coverage, and other pathways into care.
